You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0284.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

args.command:
cat > build_molecule.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
from rdkit.Geometry import Point3D

# Atom positions and connectivity transcribed from the supplied drawing.
xy={1:(315,694),2:(211,754),3:(211,875),4:(315,935),5:(420,875),6:(524,935),7:(628,875),8:(628,754),9:(524,694),10:(420,755),11:(524,575),12:(628,515),13:(731,575),14:(731,695),15:(846,732),16:(916,635),17:(846,538),18:(731,461),19:(420,641),20:(883,422),21:(798,340),22:(999,391),23:(1030,275),24:(1146,244),25:(1176,129),26:(1090,43),27:(1282,100),28:(106,935),29:(628,640),30:(524,808),31:(731,808),32:(960,538)}
rw=Chem.RWMol()
idx={}
for n in range(1,33):
    idx[n]=rw.AddAtom(Chem.Atom('C' if n<=27 else 'O' if n==28 else 'H'))
edges=[(1,2),(2,3),(3,4),(4,5),(5,10),(10,1),(5,6),(6,7),(7,8),(8,9),(9,10),(9,11),(11,12),(12,13),(13,14),(14,8),(14,15),(15,16),(16,17),(17,13),(13,18),(10,19),(17,20),(20,21),(20,22),(22,23),(23,24),(24,25),(25,26),(25,27),(3,28),(8,29),(9,30),(14,31),(17,32)]
for a,b in edges:
    rw.AddBond(idx[a],idx[b],Chem.BondType.DOUBLE if (a,b)==(5,6) else Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
mol=rw.GetMol()
Chem.SanitizeMol(mol)
conf=Chem.Conformer(mol.GetNumAtoms())
conf.Set3D(False)
for n,(x,y) in xy.items():
    conf.SetAtomPosition(idx[n],Point3D(x/100,-y/100,0))
mol.AddConformer(conf)
for a,b,direction in [(3,28,Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE),(10,19,Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE),(13,18,Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE),(8,29,Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE),(9,30,Chem.BondDir.BEGINDASH),(14,31,Chem.BondDir.BEGINDASH),(17,32,Chem.BondDir.BEGINDASH),(20,21,Chem.BondDir.BEGINDASH)]:
    bond=mol.GetBondBetweenAtoms(idx[a],idx[b])
    assert bond.GetBeginAtomIdx()==idx[a]
    bond.SetBondDir(direction)
Chem.AssignChiralTypesFromBondDirs(mol,confId=0,replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(mol,cleanIt=True,force=True)
for a in mol.GetAtoms():
    if a.HasProp('_CIPCode'):
        print('C',a.GetIdx()+1,a.GetProp('_CIPCode'))
print(Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.RemoveHs(mol)))
# Generate complete, explicit-H three-dimensional coordinates and relax them.
mol=Chem.AddHs(mol)
mol.RemoveAllConformers()
params=AllChem.ETKDGv3()
params.randomSeed=284
params.numThreads=0
params.useSmallRingTorsions=True
cids=AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(mol,numConfs=24,params=params)
assert len(cids)>0
results=AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(mol,numThreads=0,maxIters=1000)
best=min(range(len(results)),key=lambda i:results[i][1])
conf=mol.GetConformer(int(cids[best]))
# Confirm all specified stereocenters from the actual 3-D structure.
check=Chem.Mol(mol)
Chem.AssignAtomChiralTagsFromStructure(check,confId=int(cids[best]),replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(check,cleanIt=True,force=True)
for n in (3,8,9,10,13,14,17,20):
    assert check.GetAtomWithIdx(idx[n]).GetProp('_CIPCode')==mol.GetAtomWithIdx(idx[n]).GetProp('_CIPCode')
with open('answer.xyz','w') as f:
    f.write(f'{mol.GetNumAtoms()}\nCholesterol; stereochemistry from mol_0284.png; coordinates in angstroms\n')
    for atom in mol.GetAtoms():
        p=conf.GetAtomPosition(atom.GetIdx())
        f.write(f'{atom.GetSymbol():2s} {p.x: .8f} {p.y: .8f} {p.z: .8f}\n')
print('Saved answer.xyz:',mol.GetNumAtoms(),'atoms; MMFF energy',results[best][1])
PY
python build_molecule.py
ls -l answer.xyz
